bug_semantics: The Linux CRI checkpoint-restore path accepted externally supplied checkpoint tar/OCI filesystem entries, recreated them under containerd's host-side persistent container state directory, and then restored container.log with os.Stat plus RealOS.CopyFile. Both os.Stat and CopyFile's os.Open follow a final-component symlink, so a malicious checkpoint whose container.log is a symlink to an arbitrary host file caused that host file's contents to be copied to the container log path and exposed through kubectl logs.
flaw_origin: Commit 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd introduced CRImportCheckpoint and, in one feature change, added both unsafe ingress paths (fs.CopyDir or archive.Apply into containerRootDir without rejecting symlinks) and the symlink-following container.log copy to meta.LogPath. Its direct parent 07dd4ccf3599d4c22ee679b36fda3a17f8801cc2 had no CRImportCheckpoint implementation or vulnerable lines.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com> and committer Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com>; its only trailer is Signed-off-by: Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com>, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-rgh6-rfwx-v388 describes arbitrary host-file disclosure through a symlinked container.log during CRI checkpoint restore, with affected ranges >=2.1.0,<2.1.9; >=2.2.0,<2.2.5; >=2.3.0,<2.3.2 and patched versions 2.1.9, 2.2.5, and 2.3.2.

In the validated full-history clone, git log -L 416,459:internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go at pre-fix commit af60379ff63e3a1b55fcb6270a3c30ca672b35ca attributes the entire vulnerable restore block to 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd. git log -S for the exact containerLog assignment likewise finds 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd as its first addition and only the 2026 fix/backports as removals.

At BIC 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd, internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go has fs.CopyDir(containerRootDir, mountPoint) at line 405, archive.Apply(..., containerRootDir, ...) at line 431, containerLog := filepath.Join(containerRootDir, "container.log") at line 440, and c.os.CopyFile(containerLog, meta.LogPath, 0600) at line 443. pkg/os/os.go RealOS.CopyFile opens src with os.Open, which follows symlinks.

Direct-parent verification: git diff 07dd4ccf3599d4c22ee679b36fda3a17f8801cc2 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd -- internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go shows CRImportCheckpoint and all four vulnerable operations as new additions; the parent tree contains none of them. The BIC is single-parent. GitHub's first-party commit association identifies PR https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10365, and its commits endpoint exposes only this same commit, so there is no separate reconstructable squash member to substitute.

Version-boundary checks: git tag --contains 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd begins with the v2.1 prereleases and v2.1.0 and includes all affected stable boundaries. Exact tree searches find the vulnerable containerRootDir container.log assignment in v2.1.0 and v2.1.8 (line 440), v2.2.0 and v2.2.4 (line 449), and v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 (line 452).

Canonical direct fix https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/8196411f24065533093be4c7ad874c23b06178f3 (member of first-party PR https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13626) adds copyNoFollow with Lstat/regular-file validation and O_NOFOLLOW, rejects non-regular archive entries, validates OCI-copied entries, confines content to a fresh ctrd-restore directory, and copies restoreDir/container.log through copyNoFollow (internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go lines 78, 108, 125, 502, 560-561).

Patched-tag ancestry is branch-specific: cherry-pick 570e69884650eb6b0bcee19edd812428adbac8c2 is contained in v2.1.9; 357652293053d0cd3ed565f718b0050aa662ae1a in v2.2.5 and later 2.2 tags; and 09599078f66bb98f6e83087893e3f2349b019fe7 in v2.3.2 and later 2.3 tags. Each message records ancestry from canonical fix 8196411f24065533093be4c7ad874c23b06178f3. Exact fixed-tree searches find restoreDir/container.log at v2.1.9 line 519, v2.2.5 line 528, and v2.3.2 line 531.

BIC-only AI inspection used the exact commit object at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd: human author/committer Adrian Reber and only a Signed-off-by trailer; no AI authorship/co-authorship/generation marker or bot identity is present. Advisory credits for AI-assisted independent discovery do not attribute the 2024-authored/2025-committed BIC.
reasoning: The advisory-defined attack starts with an untrusted checkpoint image or archive. The restore feature introduced by 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd allowed filesystem objects from that input to reach containerRootDir through fs.CopyDir/archive.Apply, did not restrict symlink entry types, and then followed container.log through Stat and CopyFile into the CRI log path. git log -L and exact-string history converge on that feature commit, while its immediate parent-tree diff proves the restore function and vulnerable lines were absent, making it the smallest public-history BIC rather than a later move, refactor, or release commit. The BIC is present by v2.1.0 and the vulnerable source remains at each last-affected tag. Canonical patch 8196411f24065533093be4c7ad874c23b06178f3 removes the primitive through entry-type rejection, isolated restore storage, and no-follow copying; its three direct cherry-picks are present exactly at the advisory's 2.1.9, 2.2.5, and 2.3.2 patched boundaries. The associated BIC PR has only the BIC commit, so no smaller squash member is reconstructable. Finally, the BIC commit object contains no AI marker and is authored and committed by a human; later AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is not BIC attribution. Therefore the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
